messages:
chen: Taking over evening shift. Quick summary up front: 1 active incident (regen latency spike in eu-west1), mitigations applied, watchlist + a couple follow-ups.

sarah: Thanks — can you paste the current alert thresholds and where you're tracking the metric?

chen: Alert: regen_p99_latency > 1200ms for 5m in eu-west1. Dashboard: /dashboards/regen-eu-west1-latency (watching both p95/p99 + queue depth).

jason: What triggered the spike? any deploys or autoscaler churn?

chen: Looks correlated with a canary deploy at 20:10 UTC (minor model variant with KV cache disabled). We rolled the canary back at 20:18 and scaled the dedicated pool + enabled kvcache fallback. Latency dropped but p95 still elevated.

kevin: Nice quick rollback. Can you confirm kvcache fallback is on for the affected route? command I used:
```
./oncallctl routes describe regen --region eu-west1 | grep kvcache
```
chen: Confirmed: fallback=true on regen-route-v2. Also bumped pool from 6->12 nodes temporary.

deploy-bot: deploy rollback for regen-canary (rev 2026.03.17-8f3a) — succeeded :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Alert suppressed for regen_p99_latency in eu-west1 until 21:05 UTC (manual suppress by chen).

maria: Any user-facing impact or customer tickets?

chen: A handful of elevated latencies reported by synthetic monitors and ~3 user-facing errors tied to timeouts (short window). Customer support notified, CS ticket #CS-1982.

kevin: Next steps? owner?

chen: Plan: (1) keep pool at 12 for 30m and monitor (2) run a KV cache health sweep and evictions check (assigned to @kevin) (3) if p95 > 800ms after 30m open incident bridge and consider temporary traffic reroute to eu-central1 (owner: chen) (4) postmortem if root cause != canary.

kevin: On it — will run the cache sweep now and post results.

jason: Ping me if bridge opens, I can assist with reroute playbook.

maria: I'll draft an incident blurb for CS and Docs so support has a canned response.

chen: thanks team. I'll leave the watch on dashboards and update this thread at next check (in 15m). :thumbsup:

kevin: cache sweep done — found high eviction churn on one shard, raised a ticket to eng-redis (#ENG-748). Eviction rate peaked at 20:05 then tapered. Sharing snippet of logs:
```
[20:06:12] shard-7 eviction_rate=124/s keys_evicted=430
[20:07:00] shard-7 eviction_rate=98/s keys_evicted=320
```

chen: good catch — putting ENG-748 on the incident follow-up list. Last status: p99 trending down, p95 ~720ms. Next update in 10m.
